evals.name: notifications-module-review
evals.prompt: I just wrote a new `notifications` module for the server (the files under server/src/modules/notifications/ in the input folder). Can you review it for architecture / layering problems before I open a PR? For each problem give file:line, what's wrong and how to fix it. Write your review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: A review that finds the three layering violations — direct Drizzle query in routes.ts, a concrete GitHub adapter constructed inside service.ts, and node:fs I/O inside helpers.ts — with a correct relocation for each, and does not flag the conforming repository.ts.

assertions.text: Flags routes.ts for querying the database directly (drizzle-orm / db/schema / container.db in the GET handler) and says the query belongs in NotificationRepository
Flags service.ts for importing and constructing OctokitGitHubClient and says to depend on the GitHubClient port resolved from the Container (container.github) instead
Flags helpers.ts for doing filesystem I/O (node:fs/promises readFile) and says template loading must move out of helpers (service/adapter), keeping interpolate pure
Does not report repository.ts as an architecture violation (it is the one file allowed to import drizzle-orm and db/schema, and it returns mapped types)

evals.name: labels-module-review
evals.prompt: Here's the `labels` module I added (server/src/modules/labels/ in the input folder) — GET and PUT labels on a PR. Anything off with how it's structured? Give me concrete findings with file:line and a suggested fix. Write your review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: A review that finds the three violations — repository leaks $inferSelect rows (LabelRow/PullRow) into the service and out over the wire, the delete → insert → update write runs without a transaction, and the service takes FastifyReply and sets status codes — and does not flag the pure helpers.ts.

assertions.text: Flags that the repository returns Drizzle `$inferSelect` row types (LabelRow and/or PullRow) to the service instead of mapping to contract types at the repository edge
Flags that LabelService.replace runs deleteForPull → insertMany → touchPull without a transaction, and says the service should open the transaction and pass tx to the repository methods
Flags that service.ts imports FastifyReply / sets reply.status, and says HTTP status mapping belongs in routes.ts (e.g. service throws NotFoundError)
Does not report helpers.ts as an architecture violation (normalizeLabels is pure)

evals.name: reviewer-core-summary-review
evals.prompt: I added `summarizeReview` (reviewer-core/src/review/summarize.ts in the input folder) so we get a one-paragraph summary after each review run. Before I export it from the reviewer-core barrel, can you check whether it fits how that package is supposed to be built? List problems with file:line and how to fix them. Write your review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: A review that finds the three violations of reviewer-core's infrastructure-free rule — a concrete OpenRouterProvider constructed from process.env instead of an injected LLMProvider, filesystem reads of the prompt, and direct Postgres writes — says persistence and prompt loading belong to the server caller, and does not flag format.ts.

assertions.text: Flags summarize.ts for importing/constructing OpenRouterProvider (with process.env key) and says the LLMProvider must be injected via the input instead
Flags summarize.ts for reading the prompt from disk with node:fs and says the prompt should be passed in as a resolved string by the caller
Flags summarize.ts for writing to Postgres (postgres client / agent_runs update) and says persistence belongs to the server caller (repository), not reviewer-core
Does not report format.ts as an architecture violation (it is pure)
